analysis.title: The "country of the future" take-off was postponed once again
key_insights: The US 10Y yield fell below 5.0% in a risk-off week, with 17bp of decline to 4.97%, as high-beta and AI-related stocks drew down globally. Oil rose at the same time, with Brent up 4.9% to $114.9.
The stock/bond correlation flipped back to negative. Ashmore reads this as showing how much the AI build-out is expected to underpin US growth and broad risk sentiment.
Hyperscaler earnings are the key near-term hurdle. Only Meta has reported. Google, Microsoft and Amazon report this week, and reassurance on AI monetisation is expected to be the swing factor.

Meta raised the lower bound of its capex guidance and reported strong AI earnings, but warned of an increasingly challenging fundraising environment after large capital raises by Alphabet and SpaceX and expected raises by Anthropic and OpenAI. BlackRock CEO Larry Fink said competition for capital was the fiercest of his career.

Funding stress is confined so far to weak links in the AI boom and to France. US CCC spreads are 11.27%, 8.03pp above single-B and the widest gap since the pandemic. Single-B spreads are 3.24%, with a 1.19pp premium over BB, near historical lows (c. 0.5pp) rather than highs (c. 5.0pp). Ashmore reads this as localised rather than systemic stress.

Even with bullish hyperscaler earnings, US midterms (data centre regulation) and energy price uncertainty (inflation, rates, hyperscaler funding costs) may keep markets from regaining conviction in risk assets and tech in the short term.

EM equities trade at their largest-ever discount to US equities on 12-month forward earnings. MSCI EM forward P/E is 8.7x versus a 2011 low of 8.3x, despite a nearly 70% return since early 2024. The S&P 500 forward P/E fell from 22x to 18.5x since October 2025.

Brazil's Lula was re-elected for a fourth term with 51.76% to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.24%, the first time since 1989 that a first-round leader lost the run-off. Congress is dominated by Bolsonaro's Liberal Party, and there is a credit crunch and unsustainable fiscal dynamics. Ashmore says a fast move to pragmatic policy is needed to anchor the risk premium and currency, and hopes for a bigger role for VP Alckmin. Bolsonaro's annulment request is unlikely to succeed.

Moody's kept France at Aa3 with a negative outlook, assuming a deficit-reducing 2027 budget is adopted and financing costs and social tensions ease. French assets got relief after weekend protests passed without serious incidents.

This week's central bank meetings: US, Europe, Japan, Canada and New Zealand. Canada and New Zealand are expected to hike 25bp. EM meetings are in Chile, Colombia, Thailand and Egypt. Israel's election is on Tuesday.

Putin agreed in principle to three-way ceasefire talks at negotiating-team level, possibly in Abu Dhabi. The Kremlin points to mid-November and Kyiv wants early November. The sides remain far apart, and Lavrov ruled out political concessions.

Trump says he will not strike Iran before the 3 November midterms, but the military build-up continues. Ashmore sees the nearer-term risk with the Houthis rather than Iran. Iran's foreign minister restated a seven-day plan in which Hormuz reopens on day six.

The Bank of Korea held at 3.00% unanimously after hikes in July and August. September CPI was 2.9% y/y against a 2.0% target. It signalled 2026 and 2027 growth well above its August forecasts of 3.3% and 2.9%. Markets expect another 25bp hike on 26 November.

China Q3 GDP was 4.5% y/y versus a 4.4% survey, driven by exports and industry with weak consumption. South Korea's 20-day October exports rose 105.4% y/y, with chip exports up 222% to a record 45% of the total.
Türkiye cut its one-week repo rate to 36.00% from 37.00%, the first cut since January. S&P said the September investment fund crisis, involving about USD 18bn of funds, has been contained.
Egypt's pound hit a record low of 55.3 per USD. The central bank is expected to hold rates on 29 October.

UK September CPI was 3.5% y/y versus 3.4% expected, with motor fuels up 30% y/y. Markets price a November hike above 90%. US pending home sales fell 7.3% m/m to a record low as mortgage rates reached 7.6%.
EM equities fell 2.6% on the week, with China down 4.5%. EM local bonds fell 0.3%, and EM USD sovereign spreads widened. Gold fell 3.2% and Bitcoin fell 5.4% to $80,015.

sector_views.rationale: EM trades at its largest-ever forward P/E discount to US stocks (8.7x), near the 2011 low of 8.3x, while earnings expectations are revised higher.
Hyperscaler earnings may improve sentiment, but funding conditions, midterms and energy prices could limit conviction in the short term.

earnings_insights: Meta reported positive results: it raised the lower bound of future capex guidance and reported strong AI earnings. It also flagged tightening funding markets for AI capital raising.
Google, Microsoft and Amazon report this week. Reassurance on AI monetisation is expected to be the swing factor for sentiment.
Earnings expectations are being revised higher, which has compressed valuations. The S&P 500 forward P/E fell from 22x to 18.5x since October 2025.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The yield fell below 5% in a risk-off move alongside falling tech stocks, even as oil rose.
Concerns about escalation in the Middle East rose again.
Record low as mortgage rates climbed to 7.6%.
Sentiment beat expectations from a low level.
Motor fuels up 30% y/y drove the rise. Services hit 3.7% and markets price a November hike above 90%.
Exports and industry drove growth while consumption was weak, keeping Beijing on track for its 4.5-5% target.
Pause after 25bp hikes in July and August. Markets expect another 25bp hike on 26 November.
Chip exports up 222% to a record, 45% of the total.
First cut since January, with cautious guidance.
Electricity and airfares fell, offsetting a jump in food prices.
Fuel up 28% y/y added 1.5pp, food only 1.2%. Core CPI was 4.0%, below the 4.1% survey.
Lula re-elected, but faces a Congress dominated by the opposition Liberal Party.

crypto_views: Bitcoin fell 5.4% on the week to $80,015 and is down 4.3% month to date and 29% over one year.
risk_factors: Tightening funding markets for AI investment, with capital increasingly the main bottleneck to data centre expansion.
US midterms on 3 November with implications for data centre regulation.
Energy price uncertainty feeding into inflation, rates and hyperscaler funding costs.
Middle East escalation, with the Houthis the nearer-term risk.
Brazil fiscal dynamics and a divided government under Lula.
France's 2027 budget and social tensions, with Moody's outlook negative.
Egypt currency pressure and portfolio outflows.
vol_and_positioning: VIX futures stand at 19.6%, up 1.4% on the week.
The stock/bond correlation turned negative again as 10Y yields fell alongside tech drawdowns.
US CCC spreads are at 11.27%, 8.03pp above single-B, the widest gap since the pandemic. Single-B spreads are 3.24%.
US stocks fell 0.5% on the week, led by semiconductors as AI credit spreads widened.
geopolitical: Brazil: Lula re-elected for a fourth term, 51.76% to 48.24%. Flávio Bolsonaro called for annulment after the Supreme Court ordered polling stations to stay open past regular hours.

Russia-Ukraine: Witkoff met Putin in St Petersburg on 21 October after meeting Zelenskyy and the Norwegian and Finnish leaders in Oslo. Putin agreed in principle to three-way talks, possibly in Abu Dhabi. The US curbed intelligence sharing and slowed Starlink for Ukraine.

Iran: Trump says no strike before the 3 November midterms, but the build-up continues. The State Department ordered non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia on 21 October and the UK is sending Typhoon jets to Saudi Arabia.
Houthis: Trump is reportedly weighing direct strikes. A Houthi attack on 10 October killed at least 13 and injured more than 300 in Riyadh, the deadliest attack on Saudi Arabia in over a decade.
Iran's foreign minister Araghchi restated a seven-day plan in which the Strait of Hormuz reopens on day six and final deal talks resume on day seven.
Serbia: Vučić conceded defeat to the student-led Student List in the snap parliamentary election.
Venezuela: María Corina Machado returned amid US-sponsored political talks.
France: protests over the weekend did not lead to serious incidents.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler earnings this week may reassure on AI monetisation. Meta raised its capex guidance floor and reported strong AI earnings, and funding stress is limited to weak links, with single-B spreads at 3.24%.
tension_points.bear_case: Meta warned of an increasingly challenging fundraising environment. CCC spreads are at 11.27%, the widest gap to single-B since the pandemic, and capital is the main bottleneck to data centre expansion.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A disappointing AI monetisation message from Google, Microsoft or Amazon this week, or stress spreading from CCC to single-B credit.

theme_stances.key_argument: Capital is increasingly the most pressing bottleneck to data centre expansion, so AI monetisation reassurance is the swing factor.
